newsitem.title: USA: Emcare agrees to settle with Justice Dep't.
newsitem.headline: Emcare agrees to settle with Justice Dep't.

text.p: EmCare Holdings Inc said Wednesday it reached an agreement in principle with the U.S. Department of Justice to settle allegations of improper billing charges for emergency hospital services reimbursed under various programs, including Medicare and Medicaid.
EmCare said that, under the agreement, the Department of Justice's civil complaint will be dismissed.
The civil complaint was filed against Emergency Physician Billing Services Inc, an outside vendor which provided billing services on contract basis for EmCare and others, it said.

EmCare said it does not admit any of the allegations in the Department of Justice lawsuit, or any related liability. It said it anticipates the settlement will insure its rights to participate fully in Medicare, Medicaid, CAMPUS and federal employees health benefit programs.
Under the agreement in principle, it said it will pay $7.75 million to the U.S. government and various states, plus an additional $250,000 as attorneys' fees.
Leonard Riggs, chairman and chief executive officer of EmCare, said the company was pleased to have reached the agreement in principle to settle the matter amicably.
It said the settlement would allow the company to focus on developing its business, without the distraction, expense and uncertainties of continuing with the litigation.
He said billing functions will now be handled by a billing company it acquired in September 1995 and no longer the independent contractor involved in the lawsuit.
"Emcare has implemented a strict compliance program which we believe will prevent any serious billing discrepancies in he future," he said.
Emcare provides physician services management in emergency departments of hospitals.
